spec.description: Single-screen summary of a benchmark run: k6 load generator results, PostgreSQL, host metrics for every machine involved, and authentik's own CPU and heap profiles. Read it top to bottom - the k6 section says what the run achieved, the sections below say what stopped it going faster.
Login flows and HTTP requests per second. The ratio between the two is the number of requests a flow takes.
spec.title: Throughput

spec.description: Active VUs against the configured ceiling. k6 reports these without scenario labels, so they are not filtered by $scenario.
spec.title: Virtual users

spec.description: Per-request latency. Percentiles share one blue ramp (p50 nearest the background, p99 brightest); the mean is a different kind of statistic so it gets its own hue.
spec.title: HTTP request duration

spec.description: End-to-end time for a whole login flow, i.e. one k6 iteration. This is the number that matters to a user signing in.
spec.title: Login flow duration

spec.description: Full latency distribution over time, straight from the k6 native histogram. Bands that drift upward show the target degrading; a second band appearing means a bimodal response.
spec.title: Request duration distribution

spec.description: Everything in a request other than waiting for the server to think. Kept separate from the duration panel because these are microseconds while waiting time is seconds. Rising 'blocked' means the load generator is out of connections.
spec.title: Connection & transfer time (p95)

spec.description: HTTP status codes returned to k6. The login flow ends in a 302 redirect, so 200s and 302s should track each other.
spec.title: Requests by status

spec.description: Failed requests split by k6 error code. 1050/1211/1212 are client or connection level, 14xx/15xx mirror the HTTP status the server returned.
spec.title: Errors by k6 error code

spec.description: Bytes on the wire as measured by the load generator.
spec.title: Data throughput

spec.description: Completed login flows per second - one k6 iteration is one full flow.
spec.title: Logins/s

spec.description: Backends in use as a share of max_connections. Saturation here caps throughput no matter how fast the queries are.
spec.title: Connection usage

spec.description: Committed transactions per second.
spec.title: Transactions/s

spec.description: Rolled back transactions per second. Sustained rollbacks under load usually mean application errors, not contention.
spec.title: Rollbacks/s

spec.description: Share of block reads served from shared buffers rather than the OS or disk.
spec.title: Cache hit ratio

spec.description: Rows returned to the client per second.
spec.title: Rows fetched/s

spec.description: On-disk size of the benchmarked database.
spec.title: Database size

spec.description: Backends by state. A wall of 'idle in transaction' points at the application holding transactions open; 'active' climbing to max_connections is real database saturation.
spec.title: Connections by state

spec.description: Commit and rollback rate.
spec.title: Transactions

spec.description: Rows scanned versus rows actually handed back. A large gap between the two means queries are reading far more than they need.
spec.title: Rows read/s

spec.description: Write activity. Kept on its own axis because it runs orders of magnitude below the read rate.
spec.title: Rows written/s

spec.description: HTTP requests per second across all VUs. A login flow is several requests.
spec.title: Requests/s

spec.description: Dips mean the working set stopped fitting in shared_buffers.
spec.title: Buffer cache hit ratio

spec.description: Held locks by mode, zero-valued modes filtered out. Growing exclusive locks alongside flat throughput means contention.
spec.title: Locks by mode

spec.description: Age of the oldest open transaction. Long transactions hold back vacuum and inflate dead tuples.
spec.title: Longest transaction age

spec.description: Should be flat at zero. Anything here is a correctness problem in the workload, not a tuning issue.
spec.title: Deadlocks & conflicts/s

spec.description: Requested checkpoints outpacing timed ones means WAL is filling faster than checkpoint_timeout, which adds write stalls.
spec.title: Checkpoints/s

spec.description: Who is doing the writing. Buffers written 'by backend' mean queries are flushing pages themselves instead of leaving it to the background writer.
spec.title: Buffers written/s

spec.description: Write-ahead log on disk.
spec.title: WAL size

spec.description: Tables the workload is scanning end to end. High rates on a large table are the usual sign of a missing index.
spec.title: Top tables by sequential scans/s

spec.description: Dead row versions waiting on vacuum. Growth through a run means autovacuum is not keeping up with the churn.
spec.title: Top tables by dead tuples

spec.description: Median HTTP request duration, from the native histogram.
spec.title: Latency p50

spec.description: Non-idle CPU across all cores. If the target host pins at 100% the benchmark is measuring the CPU, not authentik.
spec.title: CPU utilisation

spec.description: 1-minute load average divided by core count, so 1.0 means fully committed regardless of host size. Above 1.0 there are runnable tasks waiting.
spec.title: Load average, per core

spec.description: Memory in use excluding reclaimable cache.
spec.title: Memory used

spec.description: Steal is CPU the hypervisor took away - it invalidates run-to-run comparisons. Iowait is time blocked on storage.
spec.title: CPU steal & iowait

spec.description: PSI: fraction of wall time at least one task spent waiting on CPU. More honest than utilisation once a host is oversubscribed.
spec.title: CPU pressure stall

spec.description: Rising context switches with flat throughput means time is going into scheduling rather than work.
spec.title: Context switches/s

spec.description: Bytes read from disk.
spec.title: Disk read throughput

spec.description: Bytes written to disk - mostly WAL and checkpoints on the database host.
spec.title: Disk write throughput

spec.description: Completed read and write operations per second.
spec.title: Disk IOPS

spec.description: Fraction of wall time the device had I/O in flight. Approaching 1.0 means the disk is the bottleneck.
spec.title: Disk busy

spec.description: 95th percentile HTTP request duration.
spec.title: Latency p95

spec.description: Inbound traffic on physical interfaces; container veth and bridge devices are excluded.
spec.title: Network received

spec.description: Outbound traffic on physical interfaces.
spec.title: Network transmitted

spec.description: Retransmitted segments. Non-zero values mean the network is adding latency the target is not responsible for.
spec.title: TCP retransmits/s

spec.description: Connections dropped because the accept queue was full - the classic symptom of a server that cannot accept as fast as k6 connects.
spec.title: Listen queue drops/s

spec.description: Sockets in use and in TIME_WAIT. A large TIME_WAIT pool can exhaust ephemeral ports on the load generator.
spec.title: TCP sockets in use

spec.description: Runnable and uninterruptible-sleep process counts. Blocked processes point at storage, not CPU.
spec.title: Processes

spec.description: Real filesystems only. A run that fills the disk fails in confusing ways.
spec.title: Filesystem used

spec.description: CPU nanoseconds sampled per component. Read it against the k6 throughput panel: CPU that climbs while throughput flattens is where the run stopped scaling.
spec.title: CPU time by component

spec.description: Live heap per component. A ramp that never comes back down across a run is a leak rather than load.
spec.title: Heap in use by component

spec.description: 99th percentile HTTP request duration.
spec.title: Latency p99

spec.description: Where the server component spent CPU over the selected range.
spec.title: CPU - server

spec.description: Where the worker component spent CPU over the selected range.
spec.title: CPU - worker

spec.description: Live heap by allocation site - what is still retained.
spec.title: Heap in use - server

spec.description: Total bytes allocated by site, including memory already freed. This is the allocation-pressure view, and the usual place GC overhead shows up.
spec.title: Allocations - server

spec.description: Share of requests k6 did not consider a valid response. Broken down by k6 error code below.
spec.title: Error rate

spec.description: Pass rate of the in-test assertions (status is 200, login completed).
spec.title: Checks passed

spec.description: Total completed login flows over the dashboard time range.
spec.title: Logins in range

spec.label: k6 scenario
spec.name: scenario

spec.description: PostgreSQL database the Postgres panels are scoped to.
spec.label: database
spec.name: db

spec.description: Hosts shown in the node_exporter panels.
spec.label: hosts
